title: The pause line
hook: rahao means pause; it marks the refrain that holds a hymn's center

segments.voice: Yesterday, vaaja: harmonium, tabla, and the old strings. Your line was every sound has a part.

A friend is telling a long story. The details wander all over: who said what, where they parked, what the weather was like. Then, somewhere in the middle, there's one sentence where the voice changes. And I just realized, I don't want to live like that anymore. That's the story. Everything else is the setting. Good songs work the same way: the verses move around, and the chorus comes back to tell you what it's all about. In the Guru Granth Sahib, many hymns have a line like that, and the Gurus marked it, right on the page, with a single word.
screen: `THE SENTENCE WHERE THE VOICE CHANGES.` → `THE CHORUS COMES BACK.` → `ONE WORD MARKS IT.`

segments.voice: Rahao. It means pause, or stay, or dwell here. In many shabads of the Guru Granth Sahib, it's written after a line or a couplet, like a little flag. That's the rahao line, and it holds the hymn's center. Many Sikh teachers give this key for reading a shabad: find the rahao first. The other verses are often questions, pictures, examples, stories. The rahao line is the main thought they all circle around. Read it, and the rest falls into place. It's the point of the friend's story, the thing to take home. And in kirtan you can hear it. When a shabad is sung, the rahao line usually becomes the refrain. The singers go out into a verse, then come back to the rahao, again and again. So the music matches the meaning: every time the melody comes home, it comes home to the center. Notice that the word itself means pause. The Gurus didn't just label the line; they told you what to do there. Stop. Stay a while. Let it sink in before you move on. A scripture with a built-in instruction to slow down, right at the center of the hymn. You don't need to read Gurmukhi to use this. Translations of the Granth often keep the word rahao in place. Find it, and you've found the heart of the hymn.
screen: `RAHAO — PAUSE, STAY, DWELL.` · `FIND THE RAHAO FIRST.` · `THE REFRAIN IN KIRTAN.` · `A BUILT-IN INSTRUCTION TO SLOW DOWN.` · then, large: `PAUSE HERE.`

segments.voice: If you can, open any shabad from the Guru Granth Sahib, on a page, an app or a website with translations, find the word rahao, and read the line it marks slowly, once or twice. Then close your eyes and stay with that line, without going on to the rest of the hymn. If you can't look one up right now, pause with the one sentence from your own week that mattered most.
Rahao. Pause, dwell here: the word that marks a hymn's central line, sung again and again as the refrain.
Your line: pause here. The heart of the hymn is a place to stay. Day one hundred seven.
